name: Hanoi
summary: Vietnam’s capital, with a busy Old Quarter, lakes, temples, museums and famous street food. Walk around Hoan Kiem Lake, visit the Temple of Literature and Ho Chi Minh’s mausoleum, catch a water puppet show, and eat pho, bun cha and egg coffee. Suits every first-time visitor to the north.
fee: The lake path is free. Sight tickets are separate.
getThere: Noi Bai airport is about 27–28 km north; about 40–60 minutes by car.
bestMonths: April to June or September to December
seoTitle: Hanoi travel guide — Hoan Kiem, the Old Quarter, pho and bun cha
seoDescription: Walk Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old Quarter lanes, eat pho and bun cha, queue for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, and see the water puppets. April to June or September to December is the easier window.
intro: You come for Hoan Kiem Lake, with Turtle Tower in the water at dawn, and for the Old Quarter lanes north of it, where the morning starts with pho and lunch is bun cha off the grill. Around them sit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum on Ba Dinh Square, the courtyards of the Temple of Literature, and an evening of water puppets by the lake. Stay if the city is the trip. Go on to Ninh Binh, Ha Long, or Sapa if the north outside the city is the trip.

Ba Dinh is a different morning: the mausoleum, the citadel, and One Pillar Pagoda, three gates and three tickets. Go early, because the mausoleum only opens in the morning. After dark, the bia hoi corner is Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen, in the lanes north of the lake.

Pho is the morning bowl in the Hoan Kiem lanes, including Hang Vai. Bun cha is lunch around Cua Dong. Bun dau is the plate on Ma May, and cha ca is finished at the table on Duong Thanh, with spring onion and dill. Egg coffee is the afternoon cup in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley.

South of the lake, the Opera House is at 1 Trang Tien and the history museum shares that shore. Hoa Lo is the prison at 1 Hoa Lo. The water-puppet theatre is on the east side of the lake. West Lake and Tran Quoc are the afternoon when the center has had the morning. The Temple of Literature is the courtyard west of those streets, and Metro Line 3 stops at Van Mieu.
gettingAround: Noi Bai airport is about 27–28 km north of the center, about 40 to 60 minutes by car. Bus 86 runs to Ha Noi Railway Station from 7:00 to 22:15 for 50,000 VND, and an express bus is listed at 45,000 VND.

Inside the lake grid, walk. Metro Lines 2A and 3 run 5:30 to 22:00. Line 3 stops at Van Mieu, for the Temple of Literature, and at Ha Noi Station. For Ba Dinh and West Lake, take a car or motorbike from the lake.

stayAreas.name: North of the lake
stayAreas.summary: The lanes above Hoan Kiem. You can walk to the shore and to the morning pho streets. The streets are noisy late, and Ta Hien is the evening corner.

stayAreas.name: South of Hoan Kiem
stayAreas.summary: Quieter streets around the Opera House. Still a walk to the lake. The history museum and Trang Tien sit on this side.

eat: Pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes, including Hang Vai, is the morning. Lunch is bun cha around Cua Dong. Bun dau is the plate on Ma May, and cha ca is finished at the table on Duong Thanh with spring onion and dill. Egg coffee is the afternoon cup in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley. The food guide is the menu.
interestsBody: Dining is pho in the morning, bun cha at lunch, bun dau and cha ca when you want a plate, and egg coffee in the afternoon.
The lake walk is Hoan Kiem and the lanes beside it. The Old Quarter walk covers the grid north of the lake.
Ba Dinh is the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the citadel, and One Pillar Pagoda, three gates, plus Hoa Lo at 1 Hoa Lo.
The Temple of Literature is the courtyards of the 1070 Confucian temple and the 1076 university, west of the old streets.
The family show is the water-puppet theatre at 57b Dinh Tien Hoang, on the east side of the lake.
Shopping is Dong Xuan Market, the trade streets around it, the Hang Dao weekend night market, and Trang Tien Plaza at 24 Hai Ba Trung.
West Lake is the open water north of the center, with Tran Quoc Pagoda on the shore.
The museums are Fine Arts in Ba Dinh, the history museum on Trang Tien, Ethnology in Nghia Do, and the Women's Museum at 36 Ly Thuong Kiet.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Pho, bun cha, bun dau, cha ca, and egg coffee. The food guide is the menu.

interestGroups.title: The lake and the lanes
interestGroups.summary: Hoan Kiem is the landmark. The lanes north of it are the Old Quarter walk.

blocks.heading: The lake
paragraphs: The lake path is free and open all day. Turtle Tower stands in the water, and at dawn the shore fills with people exercising and practising tai chi. Ngoc Son, on the island across the red The Huc bridge, is the one ticketed stop, and it stays open until 22:00 at weekends.

blocks.heading: The lanes
paragraphs: St Joseph's Cathedral faces the square at 40 Nha Chung, two stone towers and a clock, just west of the lake.

Train Street runs through a residential lane from Le Duan toward Phung Hung. In March 2025 the Department of Tourism asked agencies to stop running tours there. If you go, go on your own and stay off the rails.
The grid north of the lake is the Old Quarter walk: Bach Ma and Dong Xuan sit on that loop. After dark, the bia hoi corner is Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen.

blocks.heading: South of the lake
paragraphs: The Opera House is at 1 Trang Tien, columns and a dome on its own square, refurbished in 1997. It has been under renovation, so look up the programme on the theatre's website before you plan an evening inside.

cards.title: Hoan Kiem Lake
cards.summary: Walk the free lake path at dawn, with Turtle Tower in the water and willows on the shore.

cards.title: Ngoc Son Temple
cards.summary: Cross the red The Huc bridge to the island temple. The one ticketed stop on the lake walk.

cards.title: St Joseph's Cathedral
cards.summary: Two stone towers and a clock on the square at 40 Nha Chung, west of the lake.

cards.title: Train Street
cards.summary: A railway through a residential lane. Tours have been asked to stop. Stay off the rails.

cards.title: Hanoi Opera House
cards.summary: Columns and a dome at 1 Trang Tien, south of the lake. Check the programme first.

interestGroups.title: Ba Dinh and the mausoleum
interestGroups.summary: The mausoleum, the citadel, and One Pillar Pagoda are three gates, not one ticket. Hoa Lo is a fourth address, south of the lake.

blocks.heading: Three gates
paragraphs: The mausoleum, the citadel, and One Pillar Pagoda do not share a ticket, so plan them as one morning with three gates.

Start at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Visitors assemble at 17 Ngoc Ha, and visits run only in the morning on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, closing by 10:30 to 11:30 depending on the season and the day. The mausoleum is shut from 4 September to 2 November 2026 for maintenance. Walking Ba Dinh Square needs no ticket.
Then walk to the Imperial Citadel at 19c Hoang Dieu, inscribed by UNESCO in 2010, open 8:00 to 17:00 every day, and to One Pillar Pagoda, the small wooden shrine on a single stone pillar.

blocks.heading: Hoa Lo
paragraphs: Hoa Lo is the remaining prison at 1 Hoa Lo, south of the lake, with Maison Centrale still over the gate. It opens 8:00 to 17:00 every day, including holidays, with no lunch break. Under 16 is free.

cards.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
cards.summary: A morning line at 17 Ngoc Ha, on open days only. Closed Monday and Friday.

cards.title: Imperial Citadel
cards.summary: Doan Mon Gate and the flag tower in the UNESCO sector. Open every day, 8:00 to 17:00.

cards.title: One Pillar Pagoda
cards.summary: The small wooden pagoda on one stone pillar, a short walk from the citadel. Go in the morning.

cards.title: Hoa Lo Prison
cards.summary: The prison behind the Maison Centrale gate at 1 Hoa Lo. Open every day, with no lunch break.

interestGroups.title: Temple of Literature
interestGroups.summary: The Confucian temple of 1070 and the university of 1076, west of the old commercial streets.

blocks.heading: The courtyards
paragraphs: Walk through the Khue Van gate into the courtyards, past old trees and a square pond in the third courtyard. Go in the morning, before the courtyards fill. The daytime ticket is 70,000 VND, and the evening programme on Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday has its own ticket. Metro Line 3 stops at Van Mieu.

cards.title: Temple of Literature
cards.summary: The Khue Van gate and the courtyards of the 1070 temple. Best in the morning, before they fill.

interestGroups.title: A family show
interestGroups.summary: The water-puppet theatre at 57b Dinh Tien Hoang, on the east side of Hoan Kiem.

blocks.heading: The theatre
paragraphs: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre is at 57b Dinh Tien Hoang. Puppeteers stand waist-deep in the pool and steer lacquered wooden figures through rural scenes, a form dating from the 11th century. The theatre sets its own show times, so check its website, then fit the show between the lake walk and dinner in the lanes.

cards.title: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
cards.summary: Lacquered puppets on a stage of water, at 57b Dinh Tien Hoang on the east side of the lake.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Dong Xuan Market, the silver and silk streets around it, the Hang Dao weekend night market, and Trang Tien Plaza.

blocks.heading: Dong Xuan Market
paragraphs: Dong Xuan is the covered market at the north end of the Old Quarter lanes, on Dong Xuan street. It runs over three floors, with clothes and accessories on the ground floor and a dry-goods area called Bac Qua. Come for a look at wholesale Hanoi more than for souvenirs. Entry is free.

blocks.heading: The trade streets
paragraphs: The streets around the market still sell what their names promise. Hang Bac is the silver street, with jewellers' fronts along it. Hang Gai sells silk, Hang Ma sells festival goods, and Lan Ong sells herbs. Walk them as one loop from the lake to Dong Xuan and shop the windows as you go.

blocks.heading: Hang Dao night market
paragraphs: On weekend nights Hang Dao, the street that runs north from the lake toward Dong Xuan, becomes a walking street and a night market under a lit arch. Come hungry: the stalls sell snail meatballs, grilled quail, and cured pork sausage.

blocks.heading: Trang Tien Plaza
paragraphs: Trang Tien Plaza is the shopping center at 24 Hai Ba Trung, south of the lake, a change of pace after the lanes. It opens 09:30 to 21:30 Monday to Thursday, and 09:30 to 22:00 Friday to Sunday.

cards.title: Dong Xuan Market
cards.summary: Three floors of clothes, accessories, and dry goods under one roof at the north end of the lanes. Entry is free.

cards.title: Hang Bac and the trade streets
cards.summary: Silver on Hang Bac, silk on Hang Gai, festival goods on Hang Ma, and herbs on Lan Ong.

cards.title: Hang Dao night market
cards.summary: A weekend walking street under a lit arch, with snail meatballs, grilled quail, and sausage at the stalls.

cards.title: Trang Tien Plaza
cards.summary: The shopping center at 24 Hai Ba Trung, open until 21:30 on weekdays and 22:00 at weekends.

interestGroups.title: West Lake
interestGroups.summary: The open water north of the center, with Tran Quoc Pagoda on the shore.

blocks.heading: The shore
paragraphs: Walk a stretch of the West Lake shore in Tay Ho, where pagodas and cafes sit by the water. Tran Quoc Pagoda stands on the shore, its tiered stupa above the water. Late afternoon is the easy time, after the center has had your morning.

cards.title: West Lake
cards.summary: Open water and the Tay Ho shore north of the center. Best in the late afternoon.

interestGroups.title: Museums
interestGroups.summary: Four museums with their own tickets: Fine Arts, history, ethnology, and the Women's Museum.

blocks.heading: In the center
paragraphs: Fine Arts is at 66 Nguyen Thai Hoc, a short walk from the Temple of Literature. It opened to the public in 1966, and about 2,000 works are on display from a collection of nearly 20,000.
The National Museum of History is one ticket for two buildings, 1 Trang Tien and 216 Tran Quang Khai. An adult pays 40,000 VND. It opens 8:00 to 12:00 and 13:30 to 17:00, and it may close on Mondays.
The Women's Museum is at 36 Ly Thuong Kiet, open 8:00 to 17:00 every day. An adult pays 40,000 VND. It is the museum to keep for a Monday.

blocks.heading: Nghia Do
paragraphs: The Museum of Ethnology is on Nguyen Van Huyen, Nghia Do. Galleries cover Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, and the outdoor ground holds full-size stilt and thatched houses. It opens 8:30 to 17:30 and closes on Mondays and over New Year. Admission is 40,000 VND.

cards.title: Vietnam National Fine Arts Museum
cards.summary: Galleries at 66 Nguyen Thai Hoc, open since 1966. About 2,000 works on display.

cards.title: National Museum of History
cards.summary: One ticket for two buildings, prehistory to the present. Avoid Mondays and the lunch break.

cards.title: Vietnamese Women's Museum
cards.summary: Galleries at 36 Ly Thuong Kiet, including women's fashion. Open every day.

cards.title: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
cards.summary: Galleries for 54 ethnic groups and full-size outdoor houses in Nghia Do. Closed Mondays.

faqs.q: How do you get into the city from Noi Bai?
faqs.a: Noi Bai is about 27–28 km north of the center, about 40 to 60 minutes by car. Bus 86 runs to Ha Noi Railway Station from 7:00 to 22:15 for 50,000 VND, and an express bus is listed at 45,000 VND.

faqs.q: When can you visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum?
faqs.a: Mornings only, on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday. It is closed on Monday and Friday except 19 May, 2 September, and the first day of Tet, and closed for maintenance from 4 September to 2 November 2026. Visitors assemble at 17 Ngoc Ha. Entry is free on the operator's FAQ; Vietnam Tourism lists 40,000 VND.
Pho in the Hoan Kiem lanes, including Hang Vai, then bun cha for lunch around Cua Dong.

season.label: April to June, or September to December
season.note: April to June, or September to December, is the easier window. June to August is hot, humid, and rainy. Late December to March can fall to about 10°C. September to November sits around 25°C, and April can pass 30°C. Tet moves on the lunar calendar. In the days before it, seats sell out, and the first days of the new year the city is quieter.
